01 · Introduction

New city. New campus. New chapter.

Moving to another country is exciting — and sometimes overwhelming. This guide is designed to help you handle the practical things quickly, so you can focus on studying, meeting people and building your life in Ankara.

1997

Atılım University was established in Ankara.

02 · University & Campus Life

Know your campus.

Atılım Square · İncek
Library
Study spaces
Cafeteria & cafés
Sports & gym

📚 Kadriye Zaim Library

An 8,000 m² library with study areas, group rooms, digital resources and a café. The 24/7 study halls are especially useful during exam periods.

🏋️ Sports & Wellness

Campus facilities include basketball/volleyball courts, fitness and cardio rooms, multi-purpose spaces, tennis courts and an outdoor pool.

☕ Food & Social Life

Campus cafés and restaurants include Rezene Cafe, Kuşkonmaz Restaurant, Atılım Garden and cafés inside academic buildings.

University rings: current published routes include Sıhhiye, Tunus, Batıkent, Koru Metro, Eryaman and Gölbaşı. Ring stops are EGO stops. Check the Transportation Office page before travelling because departure times can change.

🚌 Morning rings

Sıhhiye 08:25 · Tunus 08:30 · Gölbaşı 08:30 · Koru 08:50 (published schedule; verify before use).

🚌 Afternoon rings

Atılım → Sıhhiye/Tunus: 16:30 on Mon–Tue; 14:40 and 16:30 on Wed–Fri (published schedule).

05 · Academic rhythm

Plan your semester.

Official 2026–2027 calendar ↗
FALL · 2026

Teaching + exams

Course registration, teaching weeks, midterms and final exams. Exact dates differ by program — use the official calendar and your ATACS/course schedule.

SPRING · 2027

Teaching + exams

Register your courses in ATACS, follow your department schedule and watch announcements for add/drop and exam dates.

SUMMER · 2027

Summer school

Summer-school registration and teaching dates are published separately in the academic calendar.

Weekly habit: check ATACS + Moodle + university email before Monday, and keep your course schedule saved on your phone.
06 · City Life & Essentials

Make Ankara feel like home.

🌤 Ankara weather cheat sheet

Official climate statistics show cold winters, warm/dry summers and noticeable seasonal changes. Average temperature is around 0.4°C in January, 13.2°C in October and 23.6°C in August.

WinterCold · layers + coat
SpringChangeable · light jacket
SummerHot/dry · SPF + water
AutumnCool evenings · layers

For the actual forecast, check the Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM).

08 · Residence Permit

Student residence permit checklist.

If you will stay in Türkiye longer than your visa/visa-exemption period or more than 90 days, you generally need a residence permit. Atılım’s Student Affairs Directorate collects the required documents and forwards student files to the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management.

Residence permit application formComplete through the official e-İkamet system; follow the appointment/print instructions.
Passport / passport substituteOriginal + required copies.
Student status documentObtain your student certificate as required.
4 biometric photographsRecent biometric-format photos.
Valid health insuranceGSS or private insurance covering the requested period, as applicable.
Proof of addressRental contract, dormitory document, title deed or other accepted evidence depending on where you live.
Residence permit fee receiptKeep the official payment receipt.
Submit to Student AffairsAtılım’s current instructions say international students should submit the requested documents to Student Affairs for forwarding.
Important: requirements can change. Always verify your exact case on e-İkamet and the Presidency of Migration Management. For questions about residence permits, YİMER 157 provides information in Turkish, English, Arabic, Russian and Farsi.

11 · AIC

Atılım International Club is always here.

“You are not just studying in Ankara. You are building a life here.”

AIC connects international students, helps newcomers navigate university life, creates social and cultural activities, and gives students a friendly first point of contact when something feels confusing.

Follow AIC: @atilim.international.club ↗

When should you contact AIC?

• You have just arrived and do not know where to start
• You need help understanding campus systems
• You want to meet students from different countries
• You are looking for events, clubs or activities
• You need someone to point you toward the right university office
• You simply want to feel less alone in a new city

One rule: if we cannot solve the issue ourselves, we help you find the right person or office.

12 · Conclusion

You belong here.

Give yourself time. Learn the city, ask questions, make friends, join something, and do not be afraid of making mistakes in Turkish. University life is not only about grades — it is also about the people and experiences you collect along the way.

We wish you a successful, safe and unforgettable journey at Atılım University. Welcome to Ankara — and welcome to our community. ❤️
